title: Recursive interface: coalesce restoration with cancelling readers
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Five children can each read and negate a dirty workspace, yet share one final restoration. With reader coefficients `[1,1,1,-1,1]`, both eager and deferred execution add `3W` to the data and restore `W`. The restoration bill falls from five negations to one. Requiring a checkpoint after child two raises the optimum back to five.

This **recursive-interface construction and tooling result** corrects PR1155's claim that read-free children are necessary. It adds a 73-line planner, a necessary and sufficient interval criterion, a proof of the minimum over checkpoint-correct partitions, and a complete conditional node bill. Every chosen cut must reproduce eager data and workspace. The implemented domain is exact integer diagonal readers and signs with fixed additive restoration prices. No supplier adoption, runtime improvement or new kappa is claimed.

[Construction, proof and recurrence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/240ab1ef40d2f22c04f162d02bd6e54df47f04ef/research/reader-restoration-cuts-seed53/README.md). Physical routing/frame admission, whole-call hosting, numerical precision beyond the exact integer model and analytic transfer remain open.

## Task and overlap

Base: `1b59b624d21924f8e3537cdc1ac52d3be6eda2fe`. Assignment seed 53, recursive interfaces. Scope key: `restoration-coalescing/diagonal-readers/checkpoint-correct-cuts`.

The closest predecessor is [PR1155](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1155) at `9821c6e9388f3fc097e94b72be9fa7b41a849527`. Its original certificate and valid failing-reader example still pass. Its unchanged interpreter also confirms this new counterexample. PR249/309's dirty-response algebra is credited; linear cancellation is not claimed as a new discovery. The new evidence is the applicability correction, observation boundary and independently checked cut planner.

[Task card and rejected covered candidates](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/240ab1ef40d2f22c04f162d02bd6e54df47f04ef/research/reader-restoration-cuts-seed53/CLAIM.md) · [exact source pins](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/240ab1ef40d2f22c04f162d02bd6e54df47f04ef/research/reader-restoration-cuts-seed53/SOURCES.json). The final pre-submission check covered 808 open PRs through #1196 and current discussions. No matching correction or planner appeared. Fetched upstream main remained at the investigation base.

## Validation

```sh
rtk proxy python3 -I -O -B research/reader-restoration-cuts-seed53/verify.py
rtk proxy python3 -I -O -B research/reader-restoration-cuts-seed53/test_package.py
```

Expected: `PASS_READER_RESTORATION_CUTS restoration=5->1 forced_cut=5 exhaustive=2851 seeded=160`, then `PASS_READER_CUT_PACKAGE` with relocation, regeneration and four corruption controls passing.

CPython 3.11.15 and 3.14.8 pass normal and optimized replay. The independent literal-column oracle checks 19,167 partitions across 2,851 exhaustive small batches and 160 seeded longer batches. Checks include the complete dirty state at every cut, literal inversion, a counted scalar invoice, mathematical failure controls, nine invalid inputs and four corrupted files. These finite checks support the written argument; they are not formal verification of the multiplication theorem.

[Validation record](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/240ab1ef40d2f22c04f162d02bd6e54df47f04ef/research/reader-restoration-cuts-seed53/VALIDATION.md) · [exact certificate](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/240ab1ef40d2f22c04f162d02bd6e54df47f04ef/research/reader-restoration-cuts-seed53/CERTIFICATE.json). Selected-record integrity and 25 related tests pass. Full cold replay, Linux execution, formalization and independent human review were not performed. Only this new research directory is added.
